scope: independent source review and local HTTP fixtures only; no production credential mutations or external provider calls

findings.issue: Removing a routed OAuth model originally invalidated config after adapter mutation, leaving the old source enabled.
findings.resolution: Preserve reviewed routes and declarations, disable affected connection when pruning cannot validate, and keep unrelated provider scopes isolated.

findings.issue: A successful or ambiguously acknowledged credential deletion/status change followed by local commit failure previously left remote and local state inconsistent.
findings.resolution: Capture exact prior credential/status in memory before mutation, hold reloadMu through bounded compensation, restore using a cleanup context independent of cancellation, confirm status and effective config, and distinguish completed rollback from incomplete rollback without leaking secrets.

findings.issue: enable/cancelled returned HTTP 200 when apply completed before cancellation and catalog refresh swallowed context cancellation; unchanged disabled pool config bypassed rollback.
findings.expected: HTTP 502 oauth_credential_change_rolled_back and original disabled state restored
findings.observed: HTTP 200 disabled=false ok=true pool_ready=false with catalog refresh warning
findings.resolution_request: Return ctx.Err after mutation and discovery before committing, so canceled work compensates.

limits: Local fixtures prove transaction and request behavior only; actual provider grants were not revoked, deleted, disabled or restored by this review.
If adapter or filesystem recovery remains unavailable, oauth_credential_rollback_incomplete explicitly requires restoring connectivity/write access and inspecting state before retrying.
Connections disabled due to missing credentials or invalid reviewed routes remain disabled until reviewed repair and explicit re-enable.
